newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea's largest union group says puts off strikes.
newsitem.headline: SKorea's largest union group says puts off strikes.

text.p: The Federation of Korean Trade Unions, South Korea's largest union group, said it is calling for its affiliates to postpone strikes in protest at a controversial labour law until January 11.
It was not clear if the organisation planned to resume the strikes on that date.
"We are postponing the strikes in order to gather our strength for a longer, more determined struggle," the federation said in a statement.
A federation official, who declined to be named, said no specific date had be set for the resumption of the strikes.
"It will depend on the situation on January 11," she said.
The federation said the second stage of strikes would be spearheaded by unions in the public sector.
"Until now, the strikes were led by manufacturing companies. But it will move to the public sector," the statement said.

"We will link the strikes to wage negotiations, work more closely with the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions and other citizens' coalitions, build stepping stones to work with the opposition parties and and fight against the New Korea Party during next year's elections," the statement said.
The ruling New Korea Party of President Kim Young-sam rammed through the labour law at a clandestine session of the National Assembly on Thursday. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5644
